doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Handmade El Saturn covers and Danny Thompson
summary: Gordon says Arkestra members made the one-off handmade covers, records sold out and were remade differently, and sold for $4.49.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Thank you. Christian do you want to jump in here?

Yeah I’d love to. Thank you, Monk. It’s interesting you immediately mentioned those handmade records and your own desire as a collector to acquire the rare El Saturn titles. Because the reason we’re even speaking with you is we were lucky enough to acquire the collection of Allan West, who rhapsodized about his memories of going to your shop and © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

said that you were about one of the only people in the country that you could get these handmade records from. And I want to ask you, what do you know about the Arkestra’s process in creating those covers. Were the musicians doing it? How was that done?

Well I never witnessed it so I can’t answer you on that. But I do know that the musicians were doing it. I guarantee you John Gilmore was sitting on the floor with the scissors cutting up stuff. But I can’t tell you really the process. I can only tell you that one day they started showing up and then the next fifteen Sun Ras were that way. They were pictures that were hand-colored, or collages that were then laminated on the covers. It was totally crazy. Every one different and that’s an interesting thing about Sun Ra, Sun Ra’s records. If they had a record it sold out right away, I would ask for some more but it didn’t work that way. He did not have a warehouse to keep his records in and an inventory manager. If they ran out of records they would just make a brand new one, a different record.
Well, ensuring the scarcity of so many of them obviously.

So I mean just as wacky as everything else they had done you know. “We don’t have that one anymore.” Danny Thompson, by the way, was kind of like the head salesman for Sun Ra’s record label. He was also the baritone player and kind of the point man for a lot of things with the band. Very nice guy. He died about two years ago now. And he — people started calling him Danny “Ray” Thompson. Originally it was just Danny Thompson, then he was like Danny Ray, and now he’s always referred to as Danny Ray Thompson. But anyway, yeah, that’s what happened, they would just come up with new ones.
So were the records being delivered in handmade sleeves, was there a standard actual sleeve for these titles or they were only issued in handmade sleeves?
Oh wow. Did those command a premium immediately in your store or were they the same price as an Impulse Sun Ra record?
